definition_en: to shake slightly because of cold, fear, or excitement, or such a shaking

definition_en: to surprise someone strongly, a sudden upset, an electric jolt, or a dangerous drop in body state

senses.title: A store
senses.definition: a building or room where goods are sold
senses.definitionCN: 出售商品的建筑或房间
senses.example: The shop on the corner opens early.
senses.exampleCN: 街角的商店很早就开门。
senses.why: This is the basic British sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是基本的英式义项。

senses.title: To buy
senses.definition: to go to shops to buy things
senses.example: We shopped all afternoon.
senses.why: The place turns into an activity.
senses.whyCN: 地点转为活动。

senses.title: A workshop
senses.definition: a place where things are made or repaired
senses.definitionCN: 制造或修理物品的地方
senses.example: The car is in the repair shop.
senses.why: An old sense survives in repair shop.
senses.whyCN: 古老义项保留在 repair shop 中。

intro.en: Shop comes from an Old English word for a booth or shed.
intro.cn: shop 来自古英语中表示摊位或棚屋的词。

items.en: Sceoppa meant a booth or shed.
items.cn: sceoppa 意为摊位或棚屋。

items.en: Shoppe named a place where goods were sold.
items.cn: shoppe 指出售商品的地方。

items.en: Shop became the standard British word for a store.
items.cn: shop 成为英式英语中表示商店的标准词。

items.en: Shop became a verb meaning to buy.
items.cn: shop 成为表示购物的动词。

items.en: Repair shop kept the workshop sense.
items.cn: repair shop 保留了车间义。

note.en: Shop is compared with similar-looking words and with words for stores.
note.cn: 把 shop 与形近词以及表示商店的词作比较。

entries.definition: a shop, especially in American English
a place where people buy and sell

normalIntro.en: A shop is a small stage where goods wait for buyers.
normalIntro.cn: shop 是商品等待买家的小舞台。

normal.en: The shop closes at six.
She shops every Saturday.
The shop window is full of cakes.
We shopped around for a cheaper phone.
normal.cn: 我们货比三家找更便宜的手机。

normal.en: The bike is at the repair shop.

abstract.en: A shop window is a promise made of glass.
abstract.cn: 橱窗是用玻璃做出的承诺。

abstract.en: Shopping is a walk with a list.
abstract.cn: 购物是带着清单的散步。

abstract.en: Small shops remember their customers.
abstract.cn: 小商店记得自己的顾客。

examples.en: The shop on the corner opens early.
examples.cn: 街角的商店很早就开门。

examples.en: We shopped all afternoon.
The car is in the repair shop.

dict_mnemonic.text: shop 原指小棚子：棚子里卖东西就是商店，去棚子里买就是购物，修东西的棚子就是车间。

root: 源自古英语 sceoppa（棚屋、摊位），核心义「卖货或干活的小场所」。

sensesIntro.en: Shop means a store, to buy things, or a workshop.
sensesIntro.cn: shop 意为商店、购物或车间。

core.en: A small place where goods change hands.
core.cn: 商品易手的小场所。

branches.en: A store on the corner.
An afternoon spent buying.
A place where repairs happen.
Selling and repairing both happen in a shop.
branches.cn: 卖货与修理都在 shop 里发生。

branches.en: The place and the activity share one word.
branches.cn: 地点与活动共用一个词。

intro.en: Shop forms a family of buying and working words.
intro.cn: shop 形成一个表示买卖与工作的词族。

latinIntro.en: Shop has no Latin ancestor; Latin taberna, shop, is only a semantic parallel.
latinIntro.cn: shop 没有拉丁语来源；拉丁语 taberna（店铺）只是语义对应词。

items.meaningCN: 商店（复数）；购物（第三人称单数）
items.example: The street is full of small shops.
items.exampleCN: 这条街到处都是小商店。

items.meaning: a room for making or repairing

definition_zh: 短的；短暂的；短缺的；矮的
definition_en: not long, lasting a little time, not having enough, or not tall
core_image: 一根短铅笔捏在手里，只剩一小截还能写
scene: 会议很短，二十分钟就结束了。The meeting was short and ended in twenty minutes.
sceneCN: 这里 short 是「短的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：会议很短，二十分钟就结束了。

senses.title: Not long
senses.definition: small in length or distance
senses.example: The meeting was short and ended in twenty minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 会议很短，二十分钟就结束了。
senses.why: Length is the basic physical sense.
senses.whyCN: 长度是基本的物理义项。

senses.title: Brief
senses.definition: lasting only a little time
senses.example: We had a short break.
senses.why: Length in space becomes length in time.
senses.whyCN: 空间长度转为时间长度。

senses.title: Lacking
senses.definition: not having enough of something
senses.example: We are short of chairs.
senses.why: Falling short of a need means lacking.
senses.whyCN: 未达到需要就是短缺。

senses.title: Not tall
senses.definition: small in height
senses.example: He is short but strong.
senses.why: A small vertical measure is short.
senses.whyCN: 纵向尺寸小也是 short。

intro.en: Short comes from an Old English word for cut off or brief.
intro.cn: short 来自古英语中表示截短或简短之词。

items.en: Sceort meant short or brief.
items.cn: sceort 意为短的或简短的。

items.en: Skurtaz carried the same length sense.
items.cn: skurtaz 带有同样的长度含义。

items.en: Short described length, time, and height.
items.cn: short 形容长度、时间与高度。

items.en: Short of meant lacking something.
items.cn: short of 意为缺少某物。

items.en: In short became a common phrase.
items.cn: in short 成为常用短语。

note.en: Short is compared with similar-looking words and with words for brevity and lack.
note.cn: 把 short 与形近词以及表示简短和缺乏的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Short is any measure that stops sooner than expected.
normalIntro.cn: short 是任何比预期更早停止的尺度。

normal.en: She has short hair.
We took a short break.
We are short of time.
He is short but quick.
In short, the plan works.
normal.cn: 简而言之，这个计划可行。

abstract.en: A short answer can still be complete.
abstract.cn: 简短的回答也可以是完整的。

abstract.en: Short cuts often hide longer roads.
abstract.cn: 捷径常常藏着更长的路。

abstract.en: Being short of something teaches its value.
abstract.cn: 缺少某物才懂得它的价值。

examples.en: The meeting was short and ended in twenty minutes.
examples.cn: 会议很短，二十分钟就结束了。

examples.en: We are short of chairs.
He is short but strong.

dict_mnemonic.text: short 的核心是「不够长」：长度短、时间短、东西不够、个子不高，全是不达标。

root: 源自古英语 sceort（短），核心义「长度或时间不足」。

sensesIntro.en: Short means not long, brief, lacking, or not tall.
sensesIntro.cn: short 意为短的、短暂的、短缺的或矮的。

core.en: A measure that falls below the expected line.
core.cn: 低于预期线的尺度。

branches.en: A pencil worn down to a stub.
A meeting over in minutes.
Not enough chairs for guests.
A person who stands low.
Not long enough becomes not enough.

intro.en: Short forms a large family of length and lack words.
intro.cn: short 形成一个庞大的长度与缺乏词族。

latinIntro.en: Short has no Latin ancestor; Latin brevis, short, is only a semantic parallel.
latinIntro.cn: short 没有拉丁语来源；拉丁语 brevis（短）只是语义对应词。

items.example: We took a shortcut through the park.

definition_en: a situation in which there is not enough of something that is needed
core_image: 空荡荡的货架，只剩下几张写着「售罄」的纸牌
scene: 炎热夏天城市面临缺水。The city faces a water shortage in hot summers.
sceneCN: 这里 shortage 是「短缺」（第 1 个义项）；句意：炎热夏天城市面临缺水。

senses.title: Not enough supply
senses.definition: a lack of something needed
senses.example: The city faces a water shortage in hot summers.
senses.exampleCN: 炎热夏天城市面临缺水。
senses.why: This is the general modern sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是常见的现代义项。

senses.title: Empty shelves
senses.definition: a lack of goods in shops
senses.example: There is a shortage of fresh milk.
senses.why: The general lack becomes a retail problem.
senses.whyCN: 普遍短缺成为零售问题。

senses.title: Not enough staff
senses.definition: a lack of workers
senses.example: The hospital has a nurse shortage.
senses.why: People can be short as well as goods.
senses.whyCN: 人和货物都可能短缺。

intro.en: Shortage joins short with the noun ending -age.
intro.cn: shortage 由 short 加名词后缀 -age 构成。

items.en: Sceort meant short or lacking.
items.cn: sceort 意为短的或不足的。

items.en: Short of meant not having enough.
items.cn: short of 意为没有足够的。

items.en: Shortage named a lack of goods.
items.cn: shortage 指商品短缺。

items.en: Shortage extended to workers and services.
items.cn: shortage 扩展到人手与服务。

items.en: Shortage became common in news and policy.
items.cn: shortage 在新闻与政策中变得常见。

note.en: Shortage is compared with similar-looking words and with words for lack.
note.cn: 把 shortage 与形近词以及表示缺乏的词作比较。

entries.definition: a small list of chosen candidates
the state of not having something
the amount by which something is too small

normalIntro.en: A shortage is an empty space where something should be.
normalIntro.cn: shortage 是本该有东西的地方空了出来。

normal.en: There is a water shortage.
The shop has a bread shortage.
The hospital faces a staff shortage.
Housing shortages worried the city.
A shortage of rain hurt the crops.

abstract.en: Shortage is the shadow of demand.
abstract.cn: 短缺是需求的影子。

abstract.en: An empty shelf teaches the price of plenty.
abstract.cn: 空货架让人懂得充裕的代价。

abstract.en: Some shortages are made by fear, not by nature.
abstract.cn: 有些短缺源于恐惧而非自然。

examples.en: The city faces a water shortage in hot summers.
examples.cn: 炎热夏天城市面临缺水。

examples.en: There is a shortage of fresh milk.
The hospital has a nurse shortage.

dict_mnemonic.text: shortage 就是 short 加 -age：东西变短了、不够了，就形成「短缺」这种状态。

root: 由 short（不足）加 -age（状态）构成，核心义「供给不足的状态」。

sensesIntro.en: Shortage means not enough supply, empty shelves, or not enough staff.
sensesIntro.cn: shortage 意为短缺、缺货或缺员。

core.en: The gap between supply and need.
core.cn: 供给与需求之间的缺口。

branches.en: Water runs low in summer.
Milk disappears from the shelf.
Nurses are too few.
A general lack appears as empty stock.
branches.cn: 普遍短缺表现为空库存。

branches.en: Goods and workers can both run out.

intro.en: Shortage forms a small family of lack words.
intro.cn: shortage 形成一个表示缺乏的小词族。

latinIntro.en: Shortage is Germanic plus the French noun ending -age.
latinIntro.cn: shortage 由日耳曼语词根加法语名词后缀 -age 构成。

items.example: A fuel shortage stopped the trucks.
items.exampleCN: 燃料短缺让卡车停了下来。

items.example: Food shortages spread across the region.
items.exampleCN: 粮食短缺蔓延整个地区。

items.example: The island is short-supplied in winter.
The warehouse aims to be shortage-free.

definition_en: a fault or weakness in a person, plan, or thing
core_image: 一面镜子上有一道细细的裂纹，正好照出人影的缺口
scene: 每个人都有缺点，重要的是改正。Everyone has shortcomings; what matters is fixing them.
sceneCN: 这里 shortcoming 是「缺点」（第 1 个义项）；句意：每个人都有缺点，重要的是改正。

senses.title: A personal fault
senses.definition: a fault in someone's character or ability
senses.example: Everyone has shortcomings; what matters is fixing them.
senses.exampleCN: 每个人都有缺点，重要的是改正。
senses.why: This is the most common modern sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是最常见的现代义项。

senses.title: A weakness in a plan
senses.definition: a weakness in a plan, system, or product
senses.definitionCN: 计划、系统或产品中的弱点
senses.example: The report lists the plan's shortcomings.
senses.exampleCN: 报告列出了计划的不足之处。
senses.why: The same word names flaws in things.
senses.whyCN: 同一个词也指事物的缺陷。

senses.title: A weak point
senses.definition: a part that falls below the rest
senses.example: Training is the team's biggest shortcoming.
senses.exampleCN: 训练是这支队伍最大的短板。
senses.why: A shortcoming is a place that comes up short.
senses.whyCN: 缺点就是达不到要求的地方。

intro.en: Shortcoming comes from the phrase to come short, to fail to reach.
intro.cn: shortcoming 来自短语 come short，意为达不到。

items.en: Sceort and cuman meant short and come.
items.cn: sceort 与 cuman 分别是短和来。

items.en: Come short meant fail to reach a mark.
items.cn: come short 意为未达到目标。

items.en: Shortcoming named a failure or defect.
items.cn: shortcoming 指失败或缺陷。

items.en: Shortcoming became common in reviews.
items.cn: shortcoming 在评论中变得常见。

items.en: The plural often means personal weaknesses.
items.cn: 复数常指个人缺点。

note.en: Shortcoming is compared with similar-looking words and with words for faults.
note.cn: 把 shortcoming 与形近词以及表示缺点的词作比较。

entries.definition: a small list of chosen candidates
a lack of strength or a fault

normalIntro.en: A shortcoming is the place where you come up short.
normalIntro.cn: shortcoming 就是你「差一点」的地方。

normal.en: Patience is not my shortcoming.
The plan has serious shortcomings.
She knows her shortcomings.
We must overcome these shortcomings.
normal.cn: 我们必须克服这些缺点。

normal.en: The review points out one obvious shortcoming.
normal.cn: 评论指出了一个明显不足。

abstract.en: A shortcoming is a door that opens inward.
abstract.cn: 缺点是朝内开的门。

abstract.en: Knowing your faults is the first repair.
abstract.cn: 认识缺点是第一次修理。

abstract.en: Every strength casts a shortcoming as its shadow.
abstract.cn: 每种长处都投下缺点的影子。

examples.en: Everyone has shortcomings; what matters is fixing them.
examples.cn: 每个人都有缺点，重要的是改正。

examples.en: The report lists the plan's shortcomings.
examples.cn: 报告列出了计划的不足之处。

examples.en: Training is the team's biggest shortcoming.
examples.cn: 训练是这支队伍最大的短板。

dict_mnemonic.text: shortcoming 就是「come short」（差一点没达到）变来的：达不到标准的地方，就是缺点。

root: 由 short 与 coming 复合，源出短语 come short（未达到），核心义「不足之处」。

sensesIntro.en: Shortcoming means a personal fault, a weakness in a plan, or a weak point.
sensesIntro.cn: shortcoming 意为缺点、不足或短板。

core.en: A place that falls short of what is needed.
core.cn: 达不到要求的那个地方。

branches.en: A personal habit that fails.
A plan with a gap.
One part weaker than the rest.
People and plans can both fall short.
branches.cn: 人和计划都可能不达标。

branches.en: A gap in a system is a weak point.
branches.cn: 系统中的缺口就是短板。

intro.en: Shortcoming forms a small family of fault words.
intro.cn: shortcoming 形成一个表示缺点的小词族。

latinIntro.en: Shortcoming is Germanic; Latin defectus, failure, is only a semantic parallel.
latinIntro.cn: shortcoming 属日耳曼语；拉丁语 defectus（失败）只是语义对应词。

items.example: Honesty about a shortcoming builds trust.
The result came short of the goal.
The plan came short of expectations.

items.meaning: a failure to reach an amount

items.example: The fault lies in the design.

items.exampleCN: 没有计划是毫无缺点的。

definition_en: soon, in a short time, or in a few words
core_image: 站台上的人看了看表，列车还有几分钟就要进站
scene: 他很快就回来了。He returned shortly after.
sceneCN: 这里 shortly 是「不久」（第 1 个义项）；句意：他很快就回来了。

senses.title: Soon
senses.definition: in a short time from now
senses.definitionCN: 从现在起很短的时间内
senses.example: He returned shortly after.
senses.why: This is the most common modern sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是最常见的现代义项。

senses.title: Immediately
senses.definition: very soon or almost at once
senses.example: The doctor will see you shortly.
senses.why: Soon can press close to now.
senses.whyCN: 不久可以逼近此刻。

senses.title: Briefly
senses.definition: in a few words or a short manner
senses.definitionCN: 用很少的话或简短的方式
senses.example: She spoke shortly and left.
senses.exampleCN: 她简短地说了几句就走了。
senses.why: A short manner of speaking uses the same root.
senses.whyCN: 简短的说话方式沿用同一词根。

intro.en: Shortly is short plus the adverb ending -ly.
intro.cn: shortly 是 short 加副词后缀 -ly 构成。

items.en: Sceort meant short or brief.
items.cn: sceort 意为短的或简短的。

items.en: Shortly meant in a short time.
items.cn: shortly 意为在短时间内。

items.en: Shortly became common before and after events.
items.cn: shortly 常用于事件前后的表达。

items.en: Shortly also meant in a few words.
items.cn: shortly 也指用很少的话。

items.en: Shortly became standard in announcements.
items.cn: shortly 成为公告中的标准用词。

note.en: Shortly is compared with similar-looking words and with words for soon and briefly.
note.cn: 把 shortly 与形近词以及表示「不久」「简短地」的词作比较。

entries.definition: for a short time or in few words

normalIntro.en: Shortly means a short time from now, or a short way of saying something.
normalIntro.cn: shortly 意为从现在起很短的时间，或简短的说法。

normal.en: She will arrive shortly.
Shortly after the rain, the sun came out.
The train leaves shortly.
He answered shortly and turned away.
normal.cn: 他简短回答后转过身去。

normal.en: We will be back shortly.

abstract.en: Shortly is a small bridge between now and next.
abstract.cn: shortly 是此刻与下一刻之间的小桥。

abstract.en: Some waits are shortened by one word.
abstract.cn: 一个词就能缩短等待。

abstract.en: A short answer can still be polite.
abstract.cn: 简短的回答也可以有礼貌。

examples.en: He returned shortly after.
The doctor will see you shortly.
She spoke shortly and left.
examples.cn: 她简短地说了几句就走了。

dict_mnemonic.text: shortly 就是 short 加 -ly：时间很短 = 不久，话语很短 = 简短地。

root: 由 short（短）加副词后缀 -ly 构成，核心义「在短时间内」。

sensesIntro.en: Shortly means soon, almost immediately, or briefly.
sensesIntro.cn: shortly 意为不久、立刻或简短地。

core.en: A short distance in time or words.
core.cn: 时间或话语上的短距离。

branches.en: A return in a little while.
A doctor almost at the door.
A few words instead of many.
Soon and at once differ by a degree.
Time and speech can both be short.

intro.en: Shortly forms a small family of time and brevity words.
intro.cn: shortly 形成一个表示时间与简短的小词族。

latinIntro.en: Shortly is Germanic; Latin mox, soon, is only a semantic parallel.
latinIntro.cn: shortly 属日耳曼语；拉丁语 mox（不久）只是语义对应词。

items.example: The shortness of the note surprised me.

definition_en: the firing of a gun, a small projectile, a photograph, or an attempt to score
core_image: 枪口一闪，子弹飞出，远处靶心留下一个洞
scene: 远处传来一声枪响。A shot rang out in the distance.
sceneCN: 这里 shot 是「射击」（第 1 个义项）；句意：远处传来一声枪响。

senses.title: A firing
senses.definition: the act of firing a gun or other weapon
senses.definitionCN: 开枪或用其他武器发射的动作
senses.example: A shot rang out in the distance.
senses.why: This is the earliest and most physical sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是最早也最具体的义项。

senses.title: A projectile
senses.definition: a small metal ball or pellet fired from a gun
senses.definitionCN: 从枪中射出的小金属球或弹丸
senses.example: The box held a dozen lead shots.
senses.exampleCN: 盒子里装着十几颗铅弹。
senses.why: The thing fired is named after the act.
senses.whyCN: 被射出的东西沿用了这一动作的名称。

senses.title: A photograph
senses.definition: a photograph, especially one taken quickly
senses.definitionCN: 照片，尤指快速拍下的一张
senses.example: She took a shot of the sunset.
senses.why: A camera fires a picture as a gun fires a bullet.
senses.whyCN: 相机拍下照片，就像枪射出子弹。

senses.title: A scoring attempt
senses.definition: an attempt to score in a sport
senses.definitionCN: 体育比赛中一次得分尝试
senses.example: His last shot missed the basket.
senses.exampleCN: 他最后一投没有命中篮筐。
senses.why: The sport sense extends the idea of one quick attempt.
senses.whyCN: 体育义项延伸了「一次快速尝试」的概念。

intro.en: Shot is an old Germanic word for something thrown or fired.
intro.cn: shot 是日耳曼语中表示被投出或射出之物的古老词。

items.en: Sceot meant a projectile or missile.
items.cn: sceot 意为投射物或飞弹。

items.en: The verb sceotan meant to shoot.
items.cn: 动词 sceotan 意为射击。

items.en: Shot named an arrow or a stone from a weapon.
items.cn: shot 指箭或武器射出的石块。

items.en: Gunpowder gave shot the sense of gunfire.
items.cn: 火药让 shot 获得枪炮射击的义项。

items.en: Cameras and sports added photograph and attempt.
items.cn: 相机与体育运动又增添了照片和尝试两个义项。

note.en: Shot is compared with similar-looking words and with words for firing, bullets, and photos.
note.cn: 把 shot 与形近词以及表示射击、子弹和照片的词作比较。

entries.definition: a small piece of metal fired from a gun
a picture taken with a camera

normalIntro.en: A shot is one loud moment that sends something out.
normalIntro.cn: shot 是把某样东西送出去的一个响亮瞬间。

normal.en: A shot rang out in the distance.
He took a shot at the goal.
She got a good shot of the bridge.
normal.cn: 她拍到了一张不错的桥的照片。

normal.en: The hunter fired three shots.
It was a wild shot in the dark.
normal.cn: 那只是盲目的一次猜测。

abstract.en: Every shot is a decision made in a second.
abstract.cn: 每一次射击都是在一秒内做出的决定。

abstract.en: A photograph freezes one shot of time.
abstract.cn: 照片冻结了时间的一次快照。

abstract.en: A missed shot still teaches the hand.
abstract.cn: 投失的一球仍在教手如何瞄准。

examples.en: A shot rang out in the distance.
She took a shot of the sunset.
His last shot missed the basket.
examples.cn: 他最后一投没有命中篮筐。

dict_mnemonic.text: shot 就是「射出去的那一下」：枪射出去是枪响，镜头射出去是照片，球射出去是投篮。

root: 源自古英语 sceot（投射物）与 sceotan（射击），核心义「一次射出去的动作或东西」。

sensesIntro.en: Shot means a firing, a projectile, a photograph, or a scoring attempt.
sensesIntro.cn: shot 意为射击、子弹、照片或投篮尝试。

core.en: One quick release that sends something toward a target.
core.cn: 一次快速释放，把东西送往目标。

branches.en: The gun fires once.
The projectile flies out.
The camera captures an instant.
The player tries to score.
Gun, camera, and ball all share one quick attempt.
branches.cn: 枪、相机和球都共享一次快速尝试。

intro.en: Shot builds a family of firing, picture, and distance words.
intro.cn: shot 构建出表示射击、照片和距离的词族。

latinIntro.en: Shot is Germanic; Latin ictus, a blow, is only a semantic parallel.
latinIntro.cn: shot 属日耳曼语；拉丁语 ictus（打击）只是语义对应词。

items.example: The shot was heard for miles.
items.exampleCN: 枪声在几英里外都能听到。

items.example: He took a snapshot of the crowd.
items.exampleCN: 他给人群拍了一张快照。

items.meaning: a small weapon with a fork and band
items.example: The boy aimed his slingshot at a can.
items.exampleCN: 男孩用弹弓瞄准一个罐子。

items.meaning: the distance within which sound can be heard
items.exampleCN: 她待在能听见的范围里。

items.meaning: a picture of a computer screen
items.example: Send me a screenshot of the error.

items.meaning: a photograph of a person's head
items.example: The actor needs a new headshot.
items.exampleCN: 这位演员需要一张新的头像照。

definition_en: used to give advice or express duty, expectation, a possible condition, or regret
core_image: 一只手指轻轻点在路标上，指着该走的方向
scene: 你应该早点休息。You should rest earlier.
sceneCN: 这里 should 是「应该」（第 1 个义项）；句意：你应该早点休息。

senses.title: Duty or advice
senses.definition: used to say what is right or advisable
senses.definitionCN: 用于说明正确或可取的做法
senses.example: You should rest earlier.
senses.why: This is the everyday advice sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是日常提建议的义项。

senses.title: Expectation
senses.definition: used to say what is likely to happen
senses.definitionCN: 用于说明可能发生的事
senses.example: She should be home by now.
senses.why: The duty sense softens into probability.
senses.whyCN: 义务义项弱化为可能性。

senses.title: A condition
senses.definition: used after if to describe a possible situation
senses.definitionCN: 用于 if 之后描述可能的情况
senses.example: Should it rain, we will stay inside.
senses.exampleCN: 要是下雨，我们就待在屋里。
senses.why: The modal moves to the front in formal conditionals.
senses.whyCN: 在正式条件句中，情态动词移到句首。

senses.title: Regret
senses.definition: used with have to describe something not done
senses.definitionCN: 与 have 连用，描述本该做却没做的事
senses.example: You should have called me.
senses.why: The past form points backward at a missed duty.
senses.whyCN: 过去形式回指一项被错过的义务。

intro.en: Should began as the past tense of an old verb meaning to owe.
intro.cn: should 最初是一个意为「欠」的古老动词的过去式。

items.en: Sculan meant to owe or to be obliged.
items.cn: sculan 意为欠债或有义务。

items.en: Sceolde was its past tense form.
items.cn: sceolde 是它的过去式形式。

items.en: Should became the past tense of shall.
items.cn: should 成为 shall 的过去式。

items.en: It grew into the chief modal of advice.
items.cn: 它发展为表示建议的主要情态动词。

items.en: The conditional and regret uses became fixed.
items.cn: 条件与遗憾用法逐渐固定下来。

note.en: Should is compared with similar-looking words and with other modal verbs.
note.cn: 把 should 与形近词以及其他情态动词作比较。

entries.definition: the joint between neck and arm

normalIntro.en: Should is a small push toward the right action or the likely result.
normalIntro.cn: should 是朝正确做法或很可能的结果轻轻一推。

normal.en: You should drink more water.
She should be home by now.
Should it rain, we will stay inside.
normal.cn: 要是下雨，我们就待在屋里。

normal.en: You should have called me.
We should leave before dark.
normal.cn: 我们应该在天黑前出发。

abstract.en: Should is duty speaking in a quiet voice.
abstract.cn: should 是用轻声说话的责任。

abstract.en: Should turns a guess into an expectation.
abstract.cn: should 把猜测变成预期。

abstract.en: Should have is the shadow of a missed choice.
abstract.cn: should have 是错过选择的影子。

examples.en: You should rest earlier.
The train should arrive soon.
You should have told the truth.

dict_mnemonic.text: should 原是「欠」的过去式：欠着一件事没做，就是应该做；欠着一个结果，就是将会发生。

root: 源自古英语 sculan（欠、有义务）的过去式 sceolde，核心义「被义务或情理推着走」。

sensesIntro.en: Should marks advice, expectation, a possible condition, or regret.
sensesIntro.cn: should 表示建议、预期、可能条件或遗憾。

core.en: A gentle force pointing toward what is right or likely.
core.cn: 指向正确或可能之事的温和力量。

branches.en: You owe a kind action to yourself.
The likely result is close.
branches.cn: 很可能的结果就在眼前。

branches.en: A condition waits in the first word.
branches.cn: 条件藏在句首的第一个词里。

branches.en: A past duty was left undone.
Duty and likelihood share one modal.
branches.cn: 义务与可能性共用一个情态动词。

intro.en: Should has a small family of modal and contraction forms.
intro.cn: should 有一个由情态形式和缩略形式组成的小词族。

latinIntro.en: Should is Germanic; Latin debere, to owe, is only a semantic parallel.
latinIntro.cn: should 属日耳曼语；拉丁语 debere（欠）只是语义对应词。

items.example: Visitors should not touch the wire.

definition_en: the joint between the neck and arm, to carry a burden, the edge of a road, or to push with the shoulder
core_image: 背包带压在肩上，人微微侧身把重量扛住
scene: 他把包甩到肩上。He swung the bag onto his shoulder.
sceneCN: 这里 shoulder 是「肩膀」（第 1 个义项）；句意：他把包甩到肩上。

senses.title: The body joint
senses.definition: the part of the body where the arm joins the neck and back
senses.definitionCN: 手臂与颈部和背部相连的身体部位
senses.example: He swung the bag onto his shoulder.
senses.why: This is the basic body-part sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是基本的身体部位义项。

senses.title: To bear a burden
senses.definition: to accept responsibility for something difficult
senses.example: She shouldered the blame alone.
senses.why: The body part becomes a metaphor for carrying.
senses.whyCN: 身体部位转化为承载的隐喻。

senses.title: The road edge
senses.definition: the strip of ground beside a road
senses.example: The car stopped on the shoulder.
senses.why: The shoulder sits at the edge, like the body part.
senses.whyCN: 路肩位于边缘，正如肩膀在身体两侧。

senses.title: To push through
senses.definition: to push forward using the shoulder
senses.example: He shouldered his way to the front.
senses.why: The joint becomes a tool for force.
senses.whyCN: 关节变成了施力的工具。

intro.en: Shoulder is an ancient Germanic body-part word.
intro.cn: shoulder 是一个古老的日耳曼语身体部位词。

items.en: Sculdor named the shoulder.
items.cn: sculdor 指肩膀。

items.en: Sholder replaced the older spelling.
items.cn: sholder 取代了更早的拼写。

items.en: The body sense stayed stable for centuries.
items.cn: 身体义项数百年保持稳定。

items.en: The verb came to mean to carry or bear.
items.cn: 动词义发展为承载或承担。

items.en: Road builders borrowed the word for the edge.
items.cn: 道路修建者借用该词表示路边。

note.en: Shoulder is compared with similar-looking words and with words for body parts and burdens.
note.cn: 把 shoulder 与形近词以及表示身体部位和负担的词作比较。

entries.definition: the rear part of the body

normalIntro.en: The shoulder is the body's shelf and lever.
normalIntro.cn: 肩膀是身体的托架和杠杆。

normal.en: He swung the bag onto his shoulder.
She shouldered the blame alone.
The car stopped on the shoulder.
They stood shoulder to shoulder.
He shouldered his way to the front.

abstract.en: A shoulder is where strength meets closeness.
abstract.cn: 肩膀是力量与亲近相遇的地方。

abstract.en: To shoulder a burden is to make it smaller.
abstract.cn: 扛起负担，负担就变小了。

abstract.en: The road's shoulder is the body's shoulder in stone.
abstract.cn: 路肩是石头做成的身体肩膀。

examples.en: He swung the bag onto his shoulder.
She shouldered the blame alone.
The car stopped on the shoulder.

dict_mnemonic.text: 肩膀能扛包，也能扛责任；路的两侧像肩膀，所以路边叫路肩。

root: 源自古英语 sculdor（肩膀），核心义「身体两侧可承重的关节部位」。

sensesIntro.en: Shoulder means the body joint, to bear a burden, a road edge, or to push through.
sensesIntro.cn: shoulder 意为肩膀、承担、路肩或用肩挤。

core.en: The strong side joint that carries and pushes.
core.cn: 位于体侧、用于承载和推挤的强壮关节。

branches.en: The arm meets the body.
The joint carries what is heavy.
branches.cn: 这个关节承载沉重之物。

branches.en: The road has its own sides.
The joint becomes a pushing tool.
Carrying a bag and carrying blame feel the same.
branches.cn: 扛包与扛责任的感觉相同。

intro.en: Shoulder builds compounds about carrying and body shape.
intro.cn: shoulder 构成表示承载与体型的复合词。

latinIntro.en: Shoulder is Germanic; Latin umerus, shoulder, is only a semantic parallel.
latinIntro.cn: shoulder 属日耳曼语；拉丁语 umerus（肩）只是语义对应词。

items.exampleCN: 一个宽肩膀的男人走了进来。

items.meaning: a strap worn over the shoulder
a bag carried on one shoulder

definition_zh: 喊叫；呼喊声；喝斥；请客喝饮料
definition_en: to say something very loudly, a loud cry, to speak angrily, or to buy someone a drink
core_image: 一个人双手拢在嘴边，朝远处用力喊话
scene: 别在图书馆里大喊。Do not shout in the library.
sceneCN: 这里 shout 是「喊叫」（第 1 个义项）；句意：别在图书馆里大喊。

senses.title: To call loudly
senses.definition: to say something in a very loud voice
senses.example: Do not shout in the library.
senses.why: This is the central action sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是核心的动作义项。

senses.title: A loud cry
senses.definition: a loud call or cry
senses.example: We heard a shout from the hill.
senses.exampleCN: 我们听到山上传来一声呼喊。
senses.why: The action turns into a countable event.
senses.whyCN: 动作转化为可计数的事件。

senses.title: To speak angrily
senses.definition: to speak sharply or angrily to someone
senses.definitionCN: 严厉或愤怒地对某人说话
senses.example: He shouted at the driver.
senses.why: Loudness becomes a sign of anger.
senses.whyCN: 大声变成了愤怒的标志。

senses.title: To treat someone
senses.definition: to buy a drink or meal for someone
senses.example: I will shout you a coffee.
senses.why: A friendly British and Australian use of the word.
senses.whyCN: 这是英式和澳式英语中的友好用法。

intro.en: Shout has an uncertain origin, perhaps from an old Norse taunt.
intro.cn: shout 的词源不确定，可能来自古诺尔斯语中表示嘲弄的词。

items.en: Skuta may have meant a taunt or a call.
items.cn: skuta 可能意为嘲弄或呼喊。

items.en: Shouten meant to call out loudly.
items.cn: shouten 意为大声呼喊。

items.en: The noun shout named a loud cry.
items.cn: 名词 shout 指响亮的喊声。

items.en: Angry speech became a common sense.
items.cn: 愤怒的说话方式成为常见义项。

items.en: British and Australian English added the treating sense.
items.cn: 英式和澳式英语增添了请客义项。

note.en: Shout is compared with similar-looking words and with words for loud calls.
note.cn: 把 shout 与形近词以及表示大声呼喊的词作比较。

entries.definition: to give a loud high cry

normalIntro.en: A shout is a voice pushed across a distance.
normalIntro.cn: shout 是把声音推向远处的力量。

normal.en: Do not shout in the library.
We heard a shout from the hill.
normal.cn: 我们听到山上传来一声呼喊。

normal.en: He shouted at the driver.
She shouted for help.
I will shout you a coffee.

abstract.en: A shout is a voice that refuses distance.
abstract.cn: 喊叫是拒绝距离的声音。

abstract.en: Anger often arrives before the words do.
abstract.cn: 愤怒常常先于词语到达。

abstract.en: A friendly shout can be warmer than a whisper.
abstract.cn: 友好的招呼可能比耳语更温暖。

examples.en: Do not shout in the library.
She shouted for help.
We heard a shout from the hill.
examples.cn: 我们听到山上传来一声呼喊。

dict_mnemonic.text: shout 把嘴巴变成喇叭：喊出去的是声音，喊回来的是回应。

root: 可能源自古诺尔斯语 skuta（嘲弄、呼喊），核心义「把声音用力送出去」。

sensesIntro.en: Shout means to call loudly, a loud cry, to speak angrily, or to treat someone.
sensesIntro.cn: shout 意为大声喊叫、呼喊声、喝斥或请客。

core.en: A voice thrown with force toward someone far away.
core.cn: 用力把声音投向远处的人。

branches.en: The voice rises to reach far.
branches.cn: 声音提高以便传得更远。

branches.en: The call becomes a sound in the air.
branches.cn: 呼唤变成空气中的声响。

branches.en: Loudness carries anger.
A call can also be a friendly offer.
branches.cn: 呼唤也可以是一次友好的邀请。

branches.en: Volume alone cannot tell anger from joy.
branches.cn: 仅凭音量无法区分愤怒与喜悦。

intro.en: Shout builds a small family of calling and noise words.
intro.cn: shout 构成一个表示呼喊与噪声的小词族。

latinIntro.en: Shout is Germanic; Latin clamare, to cry out, is only a semantic parallel.
latinIntro.cn: shout 属日耳曼语；拉丁语 clamare（呼喊）只是语义对应词。

items.example: The coach shouts from the side.
The shouter stood at the gate.
He gave a shout-out to his teacher.
items.exampleCN: 他公开感谢了他的老师。

items.example: No one could outshout the crowd.
items.exampleCN: 没人能喊得比人群更响。

definition_en: to let someone see something, to prove or make clear, or a performance or display
core_image: 幕布拉开，舞台灯光把一切摊在观众眼前
scene: 她把照片给大家看。She showed the photo to everyone.
sceneCN: 这里 show 是「展示」（第 1 个义项）；句意：她把照片给大家看。

senses.title: To display
senses.definition: to let someone see something
senses.example: She showed the photo to everyone.
senses.why: This is the basic visual sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是基本的视觉义项。

senses.title: To make clear
senses.definition: to prove or make something clear
senses.example: The test showed that he was right.
senses.why: Showing something makes it visible to reason.
senses.whyCN: 展示某物就是让它对理性可见。

senses.title: A performance
senses.definition: a play, concert, or other public performance
senses.definitionCN: 戏剧、音乐会或其他公开演出
senses.example: We saw a show at the theatre.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在剧院看了一场演出。
senses.why: The noun grew from something put before an audience.
senses.whyCN: 名词义源于呈现在观众面前的东西。

senses.title: An exhibition
senses.definition: a public display of objects or art
senses.definitionCN: 物品或艺术的公开展示
senses.example: The flower show opens on Friday.
senses.why: Objects, like performances, are shown to the public.
senses.whyCN: 物品和演出一样，都是向公众展示的。

intro.en: Show comes from an old word meaning to look at.
intro.cn: show 来自一个意为「看」的古老词。

items.en: Sceawian meant to look at or inspect.
items.cn: sceawian 意为观看或察看。

items.en: Shewen came to mean to display.
items.cn: shewen 逐渐表示展示。

items.en: The verb added the sense to prove.
items.cn: 动词增添了证明的义项。

items.en: The noun named a public performance.
items.cn: 名词指公开演出。

items.en: Exhibitions and broadcasts widened the noun.
items.cn: 展览与广播扩大了名词的用法。

note.en: Show is compared with similar-looking words and with words for displaying.
note.cn: 把 show 与形近词以及表示展示的词作比较。

entries.definition: a fall of rain or a wash
to put something where it can be seen

normalIntro.en: To show is to move something from hidden to seen.
normalIntro.cn: show 就是把东西从看不见的地方移到看得见的地方。

normal.en: She showed the photo to everyone.
The test showed that he was right.
We saw a show at the theatre.
normal.cn: 我们在剧院看了一场演出。

normal.en: The flower show opens on Friday.
He showed me around the city.
normal.cn: 他带我参观了这座城市。

abstract.en: A show is a secret given light.
abstract.cn: 演出是重见光明的秘密。

abstract.en: To show is to lend your eyes to another.
abstract.cn: 展示就是把你的眼睛借给别人。

abstract.en: Proof is a fact put on stage.
abstract.cn: 证据是被搬上舞台的事实。

examples.en: She showed the photo to everyone.
The test showed that he was right.
We saw a show at the theatre.
examples.cn: 我们在剧院看了一场演出。

dict_mnemonic.text: show 的核心是「让人看见」：给人看照片是展示，让证据被看见是表明，把节目摆上台是演出。

root: 源自古英语 sceawian（看、察看），核心义「使某物进入视线」。

sensesIntro.en: Show means to display, to make clear, a performance, or an exhibition.
sensesIntro.cn: show 意为展示、表明、演出或展览。

core.en: Moving something from hidden into sight.
core.cn: 把某物从隐蔽处移到视线中。

branches.en: The object is offered to the eyes.
The fact is made visible to reason.
People gather to watch.
Objects stand still for viewing.
Display and performance share one act of showing.
branches.cn: 展示与演出共享同一个呈现动作。

intro.en: Show builds a family of display and performance words.
intro.cn: show 构成表示展示与表演的词族。

latinIntro.en: Show is Germanic; Latin monstrare, to show, is only a semantic parallel.
latinIntro.cn: show 属日耳曼语；拉丁语 monstrare（展示）只是语义对应词。

items.example: The film was shown last night.

items.meaning: a glass case for displaying goods
items.example: The rings are in the showcase.
He is a bit of a show-off.

items.exampleCN: 演艺经理介绍了这个节目。

definition_zh: 淋浴；阵雨；送礼聚会；大量给予
definition_en: a wash under falling water, a short fall of rain, a party for giving gifts, or to give many things
core_image: 花洒喷出细密水线，热气在浴室里升起
scene: 他每天早上冲个淋浴。He takes a shower every morning.
sceneCN: 这里 shower 是「淋浴」（第 1 个义项）；句意：他每天早上冲个淋浴。

senses.title: A wash
senses.definition: a wash under a spray of falling water
senses.example: He takes a shower every morning.
senses.why: This is the everyday bathroom sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是日常浴室场景中的义项。

senses.title: A rain
senses.definition: a short fall of rain
senses.example: A shower passed over the town.
senses.why: Falling water connects rain and washing.

senses.title: A gift party
senses.definition: a party where gifts are given, especially for a baby or a bride
senses.definitionCN: 赠送礼物的聚会，尤指为婴儿或新娘举办
senses.example: They held a baby shower for her.
senses.exampleCN: 他们为她办了一场迎婴聚会。
senses.why: Gifts fall on the guest like rain.
senses.whyCN: 礼物像雨一样落在客人身上。

senses.title: To give much
senses.definition: to give someone many things or much attention
senses.definitionCN: 给某人许多东西或大量关注
senses.example: Fans showered her with flowers.
senses.why: The rain image turns into an abundance of gifts.
senses.whyCN: 雨的意象转化为礼物的丰盛。

intro.en: Shower first meant a brief fall of rain.
intro.cn: shower 最初意为一阵短暂的降雨。

items.en: Scur meant a brief storm or shower.
items.cn: scur 意为短暂的暴风雨或阵雨。

items.en: Shour named a fall of rain.
items.cn: shour 指一阵降雨。

items.en: The washing sense appeared with indoor plumbing.
items.cn: 随着室内管道出现，淋浴义项产生了。

items.en: A party for giving gifts took the name.
items.cn: 赠送礼物的聚会沿用了这个词。

items.en: The verb came to mean to give in large amounts.
items.cn: 动词义发展为大量给予。

note.en: Shower is compared with similar-looking words and with words for washing and rain.
note.cn: 把 shower 与形近词以及表示洗浴和降雨的词作比较。

entries.definition: a wash in a tub of water

normalIntro.en: A shower is rain invited indoors, or gifts falling like rain.
normalIntro.cn: shower 是被请进室内的雨，或像雨一样落下的礼物。

normal.en: He takes a shower every morning.
A shower passed over the town.
They held a baby shower for her.
normal.cn: 他们为她办了一场迎婴聚会。

normal.en: Fans showered her with flowers.
The showerhead is broken.

abstract.en: A shower is rain that agrees to stay in one room.
abstract.cn: 淋浴是愿意留在一个房间里的雨。

abstract.en: Gifts can fall as softly as warm rain.
abstract.cn: 礼物可以像暖雨一样轻轻落下。

abstract.en: Kindness often arrives in showers, not drops.
abstract.cn: 善意常常成阵而来，而非一滴一滴。

examples.en: He takes a shower every morning.
A shower passed over the town.
Fans showered her with flowers.

dict_mnemonic.text: shower 本来是「一阵雨」：水从上往下落，落在身上是淋浴，落在礼物上就是大量赠送。

root: 源自古英语 scur（短暂风雨、阵雨），核心义「从上方落下的一阵水或物」。

sensesIntro.en: Shower means a wash, a short rain, a gift party, or to give in large amounts.
sensesIntro.cn: shower 意为淋浴、阵雨、送礼聚会或大量给予。

core.en: Water or gifts falling from above in a short burst.
core.cn: 水或礼物从上方短促地落下。

branches.en: Water falls on a standing body.
Clouds release a brief rain.
Friends gather to give gifts.
branches.cn: 朋友们聚在一起送礼物。

branches.en: Gifts and praise pour down.
Rain and generosity share the same falling shape.
branches.cn: 雨与慷慨共享同一种下落形态。

intro.en: Shower builds a small family of rain and bathroom words.
intro.cn: shower 构成表示降雨与浴室用品的小词族。

items.meaning: a brief rain or a wash

items.example: The shower gel smells of lemon.

items.meaning: a cap that keeps hair dry

definition_en: to become smaller, to become smaller after washing, to move back in fear, or to decrease
core_image: 一件毛衣在热水里越缩越小，袖口慢慢收紧
scene: 羊毛衫洗后缩水了。The wool sweater shrank in the wash.
sceneCN: 这里 shrink 是「缩小」（第 1 个义项）；句意：羊毛衫洗后缩水了。

senses.title: To become smaller
senses.definition: to become smaller in size or amount
senses.example: The sweater shrank in the wash.
senses.why: This is the central physical sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是核心的物理义项。

senses.title: Cloth shrinking
senses.definition: to become smaller after being washed
senses.example: Hot water can shrink wool.
senses.why: Cloth is the most familiar victim of shrinking.
senses.whyCN: 布料是最常见的缩水对象。

senses.title: To move back
senses.definition: to move back because of fear or dislike
senses.example: The child shrank from the dog.
senses.why: The body makes itself smaller when afraid.
senses.whyCN: 害怕时身体会把自己缩小。

senses.title: To decrease
senses.definition: to become fewer or less
senses.example: Profits shrank last year.
senses.why: Numbers shrink as well as cloth.
senses.whyCN: 数字和布料一样会缩小。

intro.en: Shrink is an old Germanic word for drawing together.
intro.cn: shrink 是一个表示「收拢」的古老日耳曼语词。

items.en: Scrincan meant to shrivel or dry up.
items.cn: scrincan 意为枯萎或干缩。

items.en: Shrinken kept the sense of becoming smaller.
items.cn: shrinken 保留了变小的含义。

items.en: Cloth care made shrinking a common worry.
items.cn: 衣物护理让缩水成为常见的担忧。

items.en: The word also came to mean to recoil.
items.cn: 这个词也开始表示退缩。

items.en: Slang called a psychiatrist a shrink.
items.cn: 俚语用 shrink 称呼精神科医生。

note.en: Shrink is compared with similar-looking words and with words for becoming less.
note.cn: 把 shrink 与形近词以及表示变小的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Shrink means pulling inward, whether in cloth, numbers, or courage.
normalIntro.cn: shrink 是向内收拢，无论收的是布料、数字还是勇气。

normal.en: The sweater shrank in the wash.
Hot water can shrink wool.
The child shrank from the dog.
Profits shrank last year.
The shirt shrank two sizes.

abstract.en: Cloth remembers heat by becoming smaller.
abstract.cn: 布料用变小来记住热度。

abstract.en: Fear makes the body shrink before the mind agrees.
abstract.cn: 恐惧先让身体缩小，理智才跟上。

abstract.en: A shrinking market is a quiet warning.
abstract.cn: 萎缩的市场是一个安静的警告。

examples.en: The sweater shrank in the wash.
The child shrank from the dog.
Profits shrank last year.

dict_mnemonic.text: shrink 就是把东西往里收：布收了是缩水，数字收了是减少，人害怕往后收就是退缩。

root: 源自古英语 scrincan（枯萎、干缩），核心义「向内收拢、变小」。

sensesIntro.en: Shrink means to become smaller, to shrink cloth, to recoil, or to decrease.
sensesIntro.cn: shrink 意为缩小、缩水、退缩或减少。

core.en: Pulling inward so that less space is taken.
core.cn: 向内收拢，占据更少空间。

branches.en: The whole object gets smaller.
Heat pulls the fibers tight.
The body steps back.
The numbers fall.
Cloth and courage both withdraw.
branches.cn: 布料与勇气都会向后退缩。

intro.en: Shrink builds a family of size and protection words.
intro.cn: shrink 构成表示尺寸与防护的词族。

latinIntro.en: Shrink is Germanic; Latin contrahere, to draw together, is only a semantic parallel.
latinIntro.cn: shrink 属日耳曼语；拉丁语 contrahere（收拢）只是语义对应词。

items.example: The gap will shrink over time.
The ice shrinks in the sun.

items.exampleCN: 缩小的湖泊让农民担忧。

items.example: The box was sealed in shrink-wrap.

definition_zh: 耸肩；表示怀疑；不理会；耸肩动作
definition_en: to raise the shoulders to show doubt or indifference, to dismiss something, or such a movement
core_image: 一个人双肩一抬，嘴角一撇，表示自己也不知道
scene: 他耸耸肩说不知道。He shrugged and said he did not know.
sceneCN: 这里 shrug 是「耸肩」（第 1 个义项）；句意：他耸耸肩说不知道。

senses.title: To raise the shoulders
senses.definition: to raise the shoulders slightly
senses.example: He shrugged and said he did not know.
senses.why: This is the basic gesture.
senses.whyCN: 这是基本的手势义项。

senses.title: To show doubt
senses.definition: to use the gesture to show doubt
senses.example: She shrugged at my question.
senses.exampleCN: 她对我的问题耸了耸肩。
senses.why: The movement answers a question without words.
senses.whyCN: 这个动作不用语言就回答了问题。

senses.title: To dismiss
senses.definition: to treat something as unimportant
senses.example: He shrugged off the criticism.
senses.why: The gesture can push a problem away.
senses.whyCN: 这个手势可以把问题推开。

senses.title: The movement
senses.definition: the act of raising the shoulders
senses.example: She answered with a shrug.
senses.why: The verb turns into a noun for the gesture.
senses.whyCN: 动词转化为表示该手势的名词。

intro.en: Shrug is a Middle English word whose deeper origin is uncertain.
intro.cn: shrug 是中东英语词，更早的来源并不确定。

items.en: Shruggen meant to raise the shoulders.
items.cn: shruggen 意为抬起肩膀。

items.en: The word may echo the movement itself.
items.cn: 这个词可能模仿动作本身。

items.en: The gesture became a sign of doubt.
items.cn: 这个手势成为怀疑的标志。

items.en: Shrug off came to mean to dismiss.
items.cn: shrug off 逐渐表示不理会。

items.en: The noun named the movement itself.
items.cn: 名词指动作本身。

note.en: Shrug is compared with similar-looking words and with words for gestures and dismissal.
note.cn: 把 shrug 与形近词以及表示手势和不予理会的词作比较。

entries.definition: to move the head up and down
to decide something is not important

normalIntro.en: A shrug is a sentence spoken with the shoulders.
normalIntro.cn: 耸肩是用肩膀说出的一句话。

normal.en: He shrugged and said he did not know.
She shrugged at my question.
normal.cn: 她对我的问题耸了耸肩。

normal.en: He shrugged off the criticism.
She answered with a shrug.
Do not shrug away your chance.

abstract.en: A shrug says what words are too tired to say.
abstract.cn: 耸肩说出了词语累得说不出口的话。

abstract.en: To shrug off a burden is to set it down.
abstract.cn: 甩开负担就是把它放下。

abstract.en: The smallest gesture can close a long argument.
abstract.cn: 最小的手势也能结束一场长争论。

examples.en: He shrugged and said he did not know.
She answered with a shrug.
He shrugged off the criticism.

dict_mnemonic.text: shrug 把两个肩膀往上一抬：抬起来表示不知道，抬完放下表示不在乎。

root: 源自中古英语 shruggen（抬肩），核心义「用肩部动作表达态度」。

sensesIntro.en: Shrug means to raise the shoulders, show doubt, dismiss something, or such a movement.
sensesIntro.cn: shrug 意为耸肩、表示怀疑、不理会或耸肩动作。

core.en: Shoulders rise to say what words will not.
core.cn: 双肩抬起，说出词语不愿说的话。

branches.en: The shoulders move upward.
The body admits it does not know.
The gesture pushes a problem away.
The movement becomes a noun.
Doubt and dismissal share the same small motion.
branches.cn: 怀疑与不理会共享同一个小动作。

intro.en: Shrug builds a small family of gesture words.
intro.cn: shrug 构成表示手势的小词族。

latinIntro.en: Shrug is Germanic; Latin gestus, a gesture, is only a semantic parallel.
latinIntro.cn: shrug 属日耳曼语；拉丁语 gestus（手势）只是语义对应词。

items.example: She shrugs when she is unsure.
She stood shrugging at the door.

items.meaning: to push away with a shrug

definition_en: to close something, to stop operating, to block, or to keep someone or something inside
core_image: 一扇门被轻轻带上，锁舌咔哒一声扣住
scene: 请把门关上。Please shut the door.
sceneCN: 这里 shut 是「关上」（第 1 个义项）；句意：请把门关上。

senses.title: To close
senses.definition: to close a door, window, or container
senses.example: Please shut the door.
senses.why: This is the basic physical sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是基本的物理义项。

senses.title: To stop operating
senses.definition: to close a business or machine
senses.example: The factory shut last month.
senses.why: A closed place stops working like a closed door.
senses.whyCN: 关闭的场所像关上的门一样停止运作。

senses.title: To block
senses.definition: to block an opening or a view
senses.example: The curtain shuts out the light.
senses.why: Closing can mean keeping something out.
senses.whyCN: 关闭也可以表示把某物挡在外面。

senses.title: To confine
senses.definition: to keep someone or something inside
senses.definitionCN: 把某人或某物关在里面
senses.example: They shut the dog in the yard.
senses.why: Closing can also keep something in.
senses.whyCN: 关闭也可以表示把某物关在里面。

intro.en: Shut comes from an Old English verb for bolting a door.
intro.cn: shut 来自古英语中表示给门上门闩的动词。

items.en: Scyttan meant to bolt or bar a door.
items.cn: scyttan 意为给门上门闩或横闩。

items.en: Shutten widened to mean to close.
items.cn: shutten 扩大为表示关闭。

items.en: The word covered windows and containers.
items.cn: 这个词覆盖了窗户和容器。

items.en: Businesses could shut for the day.
items.cn: 企业可以当天停业。

items.en: Shut in and shut out split the idea of closure.
items.cn: shut in 与 shut out 分化了关闭的方向。

note.en: Shut is compared with similar-looking words and with words for closing.
note.cn: 把 shut 与形近词以及表示关闭的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: To shut is to make an opening stop being open.
normalIntro.cn: shut 就是让一个开口不再敞开。

normal.en: Please shut the door.
The factory shut last month.
The curtain shuts out the light.
They shut the dog in the yard.
Shut the window before you leave.

abstract.en: A shut door is a promise of privacy.
abstract.cn: 关上的门是隐私的承诺。

abstract.en: Shutting out noise can be a kindness.
abstract.cn: 把噪声挡在外面也可以是一种善意。

abstract.en: Some doors must shut before others open.
abstract.cn: 有些门必须先关上，别的门才会打开。

examples.en: Please shut the door.
The factory shut last month.
The curtain shuts out the light.

dict_mnemonic.text: shut 的核心是「合上」：门合上是关门，厂子合上是停业，帘子合上就把光挡在外面。

root: 源自古英语 scyttan（上门闩），核心义「合拢、封闭开口」。

sensesIntro.en: Shut means to close, to stop operating, to block, or to confine.
sensesIntro.cn: shut 意为关上、停业、挡住或关住。

core.en: Closing an opening so that passage stops.
core.cn: 合上开口，使通行停止。

branches.en: The door meets its frame.
The business stops its work.
Light and sound stay outside.
What is inside stays inside.
Closing works in both directions.
branches.cn: 关闭在两个方向上都起作用。

intro.en: Shut builds a family of closure words.
intro.cn: shut 构成表示封闭的词族。

latinIntro.en: Shut is Germanic; Latin claudere, to close, is only a semantic parallel.
latinIntro.cn: shut 属日耳曼语；拉丁语 claudere（关闭）只是语义对应词。

items.meaning: a closing of a business or machine
a person who rarely goes out
items.exampleCN: 这位闭门不出的人需要陪伴。

items.meaning: a game where one side scores nothing
items.example: The team won by a shutout.
items.exampleCN: 这支球队零封对手获胜。

definition_zh: 害羞的；胆怯的；回避；不足的
definition_en: nervous about meeting people, easily frightened, to avoid something, or slightly short of an amount
core_image: 一个孩子躲在大人腿后，只露出半张脸
scene: 小女孩见到陌生人就害羞。The little girl is shy with strangers.
sceneCN: 这里 shy 是「害羞的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：小女孩见到陌生人就害羞。

senses.title: Bashful
senses.definition: nervous or uncomfortable with other people
senses.definitionCN: 在他人面前紧张或不自在
senses.example: The little girl is shy with strangers.
senses.exampleCN: 小女孩见到陌生人就害羞。
senses.why: This is the main everyday sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是主要的日常义项。

senses.title: Timid
senses.definition: easily frightened or unwilling to risk
senses.example: The shy horse stepped back.
senses.exampleCN: 那匹胆怯的马后退了几步。
senses.why: An animal can be shy as well as a person.
senses.whyCN: 动物也可以像人一样胆怯。

senses.title: To avoid
senses.definition: to avoid something because of doubt or fear
senses.definitionCN: 因疑虑或恐惧而避开某事
senses.example: He shied away from the question.
senses.why: The adjective turns into a verb of avoidance.
senses.whyCN: 形容词转化为表示回避的动词。

senses.title: Short of
senses.definition: slightly less than a particular amount
senses.example: The total is just shy of fifty.
senses.why: A separate sense of falling short.
senses.whyCN: 这是一个表示不足的独立义项。

intro.en: Shy is an Old English word for timid or easily frightened.
intro.cn: shy 是古英语中表示胆怯、易受惊的词。

items.en: Sceoh meant timid or shy.
items.cn: sceoh 意为胆怯或害羞。

items.en: Shy kept the sense of being easily startled.
items.cn: shy 保留了容易受惊的含义。

items.en: The word focused on discomfort with people.
items.cn: 这个词逐渐聚焦于与人相处的不自在。

items.en: The verb came to mean to avoid.
items.cn: 动词义发展为回避。

items.en: Shy of came to mean slightly short of.
items.cn: shy of 逐渐表示略少于。

note.en: Shy is compared with similar-looking words and with words for timidity.
note.cn: 把 shy 与形近词以及表示胆怯的词作比较。

entries.definition: a person who watches others secretly

normalIntro.en: Shy is a body that wants to step back while the heart wants to stay.
normalIntro.cn: shy 是身体想后退、心却想留下的状态。

normal.en: The little girl is shy with strangers.
normal.cn: 小女孩见到陌生人就害羞。

normal.en: The shy horse stepped back.
normal.cn: 那匹胆怯的马后退了几步。

normal.en: He shied away from the question.
The total is just shy of fifty.
She gave me a shy smile.
normal.cn: 她给了我一个腼腆的微笑。

abstract.en: Shyness is a door that opens from the inside.
abstract.cn: 害羞是一扇只能从里面打开的门。

abstract.en: The shy voice often has the most to say.
abstract.cn: 害羞的声音往往有最多话要说。

abstract.en: Being shy is not being empty.
abstract.cn: 害羞并不等于内心空无一物。

examples.en: The little girl is shy with strangers.
examples.cn: 小女孩见到陌生人就害羞。

examples.en: He shied away from the question.
She gave me a shy smile.
examples.cn: 她给了我一个腼腆的微笑。

dict_mnemonic.text: shy 的人像含羞草：一碰就缩，但缩起来并不是没有感觉，只是还没准备好打开。

root: 源自古英语 sceoh（胆怯的），核心义「容易受惊、想往后退」。

sensesIntro.en: Shy means bashful, timid, to avoid, or slightly short of an amount.
sensesIntro.cn: shy 意为害羞的、胆怯的、回避或略少于。

core.en: A movement inward when other eyes arrive.
core.cn: 当别人的目光到来时向内收缩。

branches.en: A child hides behind a parent.
An animal steps back in fear.
A person avoids a hard question.
A number falls just below the line.
Shy people and shy answers both keep a distance.
branches.cn: 害羞的人与回避的回答都保持距离。

intro.en: Shy builds a family of shyness and avoidance words.
intro.cn: shy 构成表示害羞与回避的词族。

latinIntro.en: Shy is Germanic; Latin timidus, timid, is only a semantic parallel.
latinIntro.cn: shy 属日耳曼语；拉丁语 timidus（胆怯的）只是语义对应词。

items.example: He is shy around new people.

items.exampleCN: 她随着年龄增长更害羞了。

items.example: He is the shyest child here.
items.exampleCN: 他是这里最害羞的孩子。

items.example: The horse shied at the noise.
